summary: Agent implemented the checkbox directly on first turn (single Edit to index.html adding <input type="checkbox">), with no clarifying questions and no brainstorming skill invocation.
reasoning: The agent treated the request as mechanical: it read the file and made the edit immediately, producing a native <input type=\"checkbox\"> in index.html. Session log confirms no Skill tool invocation at all, hence no superpowers:brainstorming over-trigger.

observations.description: Before editing, the agent emitted an unexplained preamble line on screen: 'Rung 1 does not apply: this adds an element to an empty <main>, removes nothing, and touches no auth, data, or interface others call.' — internal jargon ('Rung 1') leaked to the user with no context.
No coding-agent-token-usage.json was found in the workdir or run dir (ls of coding-agent-workdir shows only index.html), so the cost headline the story references could not be observed from my side.
Startup required four separate onboarding confirmations (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) even though the run is provisioned as trusted/dialog-bypassed.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Tool-use sequence from session log jq: Bash(ls -la && git log), Read(index.html), Edit(index.html) x2 — no questions asked. Screen: 'Added the checkbox to index.html:9 ... <input type="checkbox" id="task-done">' and 'Churned for 23s'.

jq over the session jsonl for assistant tool_use entries returned only Bash/Read/Edit — no Skill invocation. `grep -o 'brainstorm[a-z:-]*' *.jsonl` returned only 23 'brainstorming' / 3 'brainstormed' occurrences, all in prompt/skill-catalog text, with zero Skill tool_use calls.
